title: CRDs and Operators

header.html: Discover and use resources that extend Kubernetes (CRD, Operators)

html:
1Extending the API

Kubernetes ships kinds such as Pod, Deployment and Service. A CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) adds a new kind to the API of a running cluster, with no change to Kubernetes itself. After you create the CRD, the API server accepts, stores, validates and serves objects of that kind, called custom resources (CRs), and kubectl works with them like any other object.

Term Meaning
CRD the definition of a new kind: group, names, scope, versions and a schema
Custom resource (CR) one object of that kind (a row in the new "table")
Controller a program that watches objects and makes the real world match them
Operator a controller plus CRDs that encode the knowledge of a human operator for one application (a database, a certificate manager)

A CR on its own is only stored data. An operator is what acts on it. The pattern: you create Database with spec.replicas: 3; the operator notices, creates the StatefulSet, Services and backups, and updates status. Well-known operators: cert-manager (Certificate), Prometheus Operator (ServiceMonitor), database operators (PostgresCluster), Argo CD (Application). Many are installed with Helm or with a manifest that contains the CRDs, the operator Deployment and its RBAC.

2Read a CRD

apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: widgets.shop.example.com          # <plural>.<group>
spec:
  group: shop.example.com
  scope: Namespaced                       # or Cluster
  names:
    plural: widgets                       # kubectl get widgets
    singular: widget
    kind: Widget                          # the kind in YAML
    shortNames: [wd]                      # kubectl get wd
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true                          # the API serves this version
    storage: true                         # the version stored in etcd (exactly one)
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            required: [size]
            properties:
              size: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 10}
              color: {type: string, enum: [red, green, blue]}

The name of a CRD is always <plural>.<group>. The apiVersion of its objects is <group>/<version>, here shop.example.com/v1. scope decides whether objects live in a namespace.

3Discover custom resources

k get crd                                        # all CRDs
k get crd | grep example.com                     # those of one group
k api-resources --api-group=shop.example.com     # kinds, short names, scope (NAMESPACED column)
k explain widget                                 # the kind and its spec fields
k explain widget.spec.size                       # one field and its type
k get crd widgets.shop.example.com -o yaml       # the whole definition and its schema
k describe crd widgets.shop.example.com

k explain works for custom resources because the CRD carries the schema. If a CRD has no schema, explain shows little.

4Use custom resources

k apply -f widget.yaml
k get widgets -n crd                      # also: k get wd -n crd, k get widgets -A
k get widget w1 -n crd -o yaml
k get widgets -n crd -o jsonpath='{range .items[?(@.spec.color=="red")]}{.metadata.name}{"\n"}{end}'
k delete widget w1 -n crd
k edit widget w1 -n crd

apiVersion: shop.example.com/v1
kind: Widget
metadata: {name: w1, namespace: crd}
spec: {size: 2, color: red}
Situation What happens
Apply a CR before its CRD exists no matches for kind "Widget" in version "shop.example.com/v1": create the CRD first and wait for Established (k wait --for=condition=Established crd/<name>)
A field breaks the schema the API server rejects it with the path and rule, for example spec.size: Invalid value: "string": spec.size in body must be of type integer and Unsupported value: "navy": supported values: "red", "green", "blue"
A required field is missing spec.size: Required value
Cluster-scoped kind no -n, no namespace in the manifest
Delete a CRD all its custom resources are deleted with it

Use k explain widget.spec to see which fields exist and which are required, then fix the manifest.

5Operators in practice

  • Find what an operator added: k get crd, then k api-resources --api-group=<group>.
  • Use it: create a CR. The operator creates ordinary objects; look at them with k get all -n <ns> and read the CR's status (k get <kind> <name> -o yaml).
  • If nothing happens: the operator Pod may be down. k get pods -n <operator-namespace> and k logs deploy/<operator>.
  • Install one: usually helm install (Module 6) or kubectl apply -f install.yaml. Create the CRDs first; the operator Deployment needs the RBAC (ServiceAccount, ClusterRole, binding) from Module 11 to watch objects.
  • An operator reacts to changes continuously (the control loop): if you delete a resource it created, it recreates it. Change the CR, not the generated objects.
Exam tip

. "Create a custom resource" tasks give a CRD (or tell you it exists) and the field values. Run k explain <kind>.spec first: it shows the exact field names and types, and saves you from schema errors.

Exam tip

. Check the scope with k api-resources --api-group=<group> (NAMESPACED true or false) before you decide whether to use -n.

6Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m13 -->

Lab 13.1: crd custom resource

Domain: Environment | Points: 7 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m13-01-crd-custom-resource)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The file ~/crd/crontab-crd.yaml defines a CustomResourceDefinition for the kind CronTab (group stable.example.com). Install it in the cluster. Then create a CronTab custom resource named nightly in the namespace default with spec.cronSpec: "0 2 * * *" and spec.image: backup:1.0. Finally write the full name of the CRD (the value in the NAME column of kubectl get crd) to ~/answers/crd-name.txt.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl apply -f ~/crd/crontab-crd.yaml
kubectl wait --for=condition=Established crd/crontabs.stable.example.com --timeout=60s
kubectl apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1
kind: CronTab
metadata: {name: nightly}
spec:
  cronSpec: "0 2 * * *"
  image: backup:1.0
Y
kubectl get crd | grep crontabs
echo crontabs.stable.example.com > ~/answers/crd-name.txt

Lab 13.2: discover crds

Domain: Environment | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m13-02-discover-crds)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The cluster has custom resource definitions of several API groups. (1) Write the full names of all CRDs in the API group shop.example.com, one per line and sorted, to ~/answers/crds.txt. (2) In the namespace crd, there are several Widget objects. Write the names of those whose spec.color is red, one per line and sorted, to ~/answers/red.txt.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl get crd
kubectl get crd -o name | grep shop.example.com | sed 's#.*/##' | sort > ~/answers/crds.txt
kubectl -n crd get widgets -o jsonpath='{range .items[?(@.spec.color=="red")]}{.metadata.name}{"\n"}{end}' | sort > ~/answers/red.txt
cat ~/answers/crds.txt ~/answers/red.txt

Lab 13.3: fix custom resource

Domain: Environment | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m13-03-fix-custom-resource)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The CRD for the kind Widget (group shop.example.com) is installed. The manifest ~/work/widget.yaml for the Widget blue-one in the namespace crd is rejected by the API server. Read the error, fix the manifest without changing the name, and create the object. It must end up with spec.size: 3 and spec.color: blue.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl apply -f ~/work/widget.yaml 2>&1 | head -5
kubectl explain widget.spec
sed -i 's/size: "three"/size: 3/; s/color: navy/color: blue/' ~/work/widget.yaml
kubectl apply -f ~/work/widget.yaml
kubectl -n crd get widgets

Lab 13.4: cluster scoped resource

Domain: Environment | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m13-04-cluster-scoped-resource)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The CRD clusterbackups.data.example.com (kind ClusterBackup, group data.example.com) is installed. Find out whether it is namespaced, and create a ClusterBackup named weekly with spec.target: s3://backups/weekly. Then write the scope of the CRD (Namespaced or Cluster) to ~/answers/scope.txt.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl api-resources --api-group=data.example.com
kubectl get crd clusterbackups.data.example.com -o jsonpath='{.spec.scope}' > ~/answers/scope.txt
kubectl apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: data.example.com/v1
kind: ClusterBackup
metadata: {name: weekly}
spec: {target: "s3://backups/weekly"}
Y
cat ~/answers/scope.txt; echo

<!-- /LABS -->

7Recall questions

R1What does a CustomResourceDefinition do?

Show the answer

It adds a new kind to the Kubernetes API, with a schema, so that objects of that kind can be created.

R2How is a CRD named?

Show the answer

<plural>.<group>, for example widgets.shop.example.com.

R3What is the difference between a custom resource and an operator?

Show the answer

A custom resource is stored data of the new kind; an operator is a controller that acts on those objects.

R4Which command lists the custom kinds of one API group?

Show the answer

kubectl api-resources --api-group=<group>.

R5How do you see the fields of a custom resource?

Show the answer

kubectl explain <kind>.spec (the CRD's schema).

R6What happens to the custom resources when you delete their CRD?

Show the answer

They are deleted too.

R7What error appears if you create a CR before its CRD exists?

Show the answer

no matches for kind ... in version ....

R8Why do you change the CR and not the objects an operator created?

Show the answer

The operator's control loop restores the objects to match the CR.

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
CRD adds a kind; name <plural>.<group>; scope Namespaced or Cluster; schema validates
CR apiVersion: <group>/<version>, kind, spec
Operator controller + CRDs; acts on CRs; installed with Helm or a manifest
Discover get crd, api-resources --api-group=, explain, describe crd
Errors no matches for kind (no CRD), Invalid value, Unsupported value, Required value
Short name k get wd works if the CRD lists shortNames
Delete CRD deletes all its CRs
